newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - June 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
HOUSE PRICES GO UP AND UP
Some of the most sought after areas in London, like Belgravia, Mayfair and Notting Hill, are seeing rises in property prices of 50 percent over the last 18 months.
BONANZA AT LAST AS THE HALIFAX FLOATS

Today's flotation of the Halifax stands to make almost one in five adult Britons an average of 2323 pounds in free shares. The flotation will at last create a genuine shareholding democracy, but many of the new shareholders may experience a rocky few days as share prices could swing wildly.
LEFT'S VICTORY IN FRENCH POLL HITS THE FRANC

French financial markets were expected to experience a rush of selling of all things French today, following the victory for Lionel Jospin's socialists in yesterday's General Election. The new government is seen as less business-friendly, and the French franc was affected by fears that Jospin might make unemployment a bigger priority than meeting Emu criteria.

Metroline Holdings, one of the last independent bus companies of the old London Transport network, is to float this summer, in a move which will mean windfalls of up to 27,000 stg for some 500 bus drivers and conductors.
